best_overlap.note: Longest stretch inside the period with the Sun and the Earth both above the skyline (nominal skyline). Optimistic and pessimistic durations are the longest such stretch with the skyline lowered or raised by sigma. Sun+Earth 'both' windows are pure geometry and ignore whether a lander would still be alive. The cost model's usable hours count only hours while the lander is alive, so they are lower.

cost_caveat: A distribution under stated assumptions, not a mission-grade estimate. Cost runs cover their own mission period (see landing_time_utc and mission_days), not the comparison period.
usable_hour_definition: A usable hour is an hour in which the Sun AND the Earth are both above the skyline, counted only while the lander is alive. The lander lands at the start of the longest sunlit stretch that begins in the first lunar day and dies at the first dark stretch longer than its battery endurance. Burn ratio = total mission cost / usable hours, in $M per usable hour; it is undefined in a trial with zero usable hours, and those trials are left out of the percentiles and the histogram (see p_zero_usable_hours).

Site coordinates and notes come from repo comments with no cited source. Add the citation to backend/data/site_notes.json to mark them verified.

The Horizons ephemeris was fetched for an observer at 0.00 km above the reference sphere; the LOLA ground height is 5.13 km. Terrain is handled by the horizon mask, not by the ephemeris. Upper bound on the direction error from the height difference (height / distance): about 0.00082 deg for Earth at its closest (356,400 km) and 0.0000020 deg for the Sun. Not yet checked against a re-fetch with the real altitude.

The best_overlap value inside ephemeris_long/*.json assumes a flat horizon (elevation > 0). It is not loaded. This database recomputes best overlap per lunar day for each horizon model; the website's getBestOverlap still reads the flat value until it is switched to the API.

The website reads the skyline by linear interpolation between whole-degree bins; the committed cost_mc.py uses floor(azimuth). This database uses linear interpolation for all visibility and for the default terrain-aware cost run, and also stores a floor(azimuth) cost run so earlier numbers reproduce.

Optimistic and pessimistic windows shift the whole skyline by -/+ sigma (0.3 degrees unless changed, a team assumption). They do not include ephemeris error, the apparent size of the Sun or Earth, or site position error.
The Sun and Earth are treated as points at their centres. The Sun's disc is about 0.5 degrees wide and the Earth's about 1.9 degrees as seen from the Moon, so real rises and sets are gradual.

STARGAZER_Project_Overview_Plan.md names 'Wiechert Circle' (and 'Shackleton Crater') as sites; the data has malapert, mons-mouton, shackleton. The database follows the data. See backend/docs/ADD_A_SITE.md to add a site; the team should correct the plan doc and slides.

meta.caveat: Geometric visibility only: whether the centre of the Sun or Earth is above the terrain skyline. Sun visibility is not electrical power and Earth visibility is not a working radio link; no power-system or link-budget model is included.
